title: Zero-point focusing makes the null-cone clock of arXiv:2611.34924 infinite
description:
The finite-dimensional Hilbert space of a causal diamond in arXiv:2611.34924 is derived from a gravitational clock quantized as a product of shear operators. Zero-point fluctuations of the infinitely many null-cone modes make that clock infinite: splitting the cone into N intervals gives a focusing lower bound (π/√10)(ℏ/κ) N2 ln(v/ε)/(v−ε)2 for every N.

In the setting the paper uses for its own state counting (corner data fixed, radiation linearized, all radial modes kept), the clock's quadratic form is +∞ on every nonzero vector, so the causal-diamond space is {0}. Both of the paper's arguments that states exist fail: the Wigner-measure step (C.15b) and the order-by-order step (C.15e). Normal ordering removes the infinity, but then the partial focusing takes negative values, contrary to the positivity asserted below (4.22).

The archive contains the proof (PROOF.md) and numerical checks. Code: MIT License; text: CC BY 4.0.
